name: Bankside
notes: South Bank strip in front of Tate Modern; one of the most-walked frames in the archive, dusk and morning both repeat here.

name: Limehouse Cut, north entrance
notes: Where the Cut opens onto Bow Locks; the canal corridor the eventual game will treat as a fast-travel spine.

name: Smithfield alleys
notes: The back-of-market alleys behind Smithfield at six in the morning; Victorian ironwork and a working market in the same frame.

name: Regent's Canal at Camden Lock
notes: The first lock of the Camden-to-Lea walk; the bridge frame here is a recurring composition across four cameras’ worth of kit.

name: River Lea at Hackney Marshes
notes: End of the Camden-to-Lea spine; the towpath opens into the marshes and the sky doubles in size.

name: Thames tideway at Wapping
notes: Foreshore at low water near Wapping Old Stairs; the river bed is briefly a walkable surface here.

name: South Bank wind tunnel
notes: The undercroft turn at Royal Festival Hall that becomes a wind tunnel at dusk; the camera-tested truth of the article.

name: Liverpool Street (the half-hour wait)
notes: The kerbside where the home-built 360 rig waited thirty minutes for a hotspot association in 2014; origin chapter of the whole practice.

name: Rotherhithe at blue hour
notes: The closing line of the 360-walking article landed here; the river bend the studio walks to when the light goes.

name: Regent's Canal at Mile End
notes: The Mile End stretch where the towpath narrows and the gasholder frame opens up; midway on the Camden-to-Lea route.
